title: Checked native-entry transitions
intro: Proposed checked entry-to-settlement corrections for the incumbent one-session CLI. C1–C4 have scoped checked evidence; native-entry transitions remain a design awaiting implementation and runtime checks. Boxes denote in-process responsibilities. Graph views start at the dark Start here node; sequences start at their first message. Historical composition views retain their fixed-reference scope.

discussion.title: Keep signal protection through every failure exit
discussion.status: Focused transition review found no concrete issue; runtime checks remain owed
discussion.summary: The front retains signal ownership on selection failure. Watching precedes both children; readers remain shielded until thread exit. Failed Started mask restoration enters real runner teardown. The complete design, exact discriminator families and conditional repair price are in docs/native-entry-transition-design.md.

diagrams.title: Publication, ending and cleanup join before return
diagrams.caption: Nominal current front path when the runner returns its own Ended. Selection is shown without protocol internals; worker wait-error admission is a separate limit. Start events and appearance polls are omitted. Cleanup diagnostics and cancellation precedence apply to supplied observations. No-ending failures are covered by the acquisition view; this is not all-interleaving or runtime preservation evidence.

diagrams.title: Acquisition and no-ending failure limits
diagrams.caption: A0–A15 refer to the textual source inventory in docs/result-job-source-evidence.md. This compact view aggregates stopping branches: early preparation refuses directly; selection failure explicitly removes the prepared workspace; partial allocator cleanup remains local. Solid arrows show control/outcomes, not ownership proof. Amber nodes mark remaining source limits. C1 retains error cancellation; private wait-error checks and front transfer are recorded in docs/completion-failure-design-evidence.md. No alternative or package is selected.

diagrams.title: Required failure facts and settlement precedence
diagrams.caption: Required repair contract, not current implementation or observed conformance. Solid arrows are decisions and outcome order. Retained runner cancellation can come from success or error; worker reap and allocator cleanup reports belong to their own resource owners. An original missing/invalid-result failure is checked before cleanup precedence. Every operational report remains available even when cancellation wins. See the completion specification and discriminating evidence matrix.

diagrams.title: Owned terminal handoff followed by failed exec
diagrams.caption: Proposed bounded correction for an interactive lease initially owned by the launcher. Checked handback requires no competing foreground transfer or unrelated reuse of the recorded group identity through recovery; CLI lifetime alone does not establish those premises. The record never authorises post-reap group signalling. All recovery errors stay beside the original spawn errno. Started means spawn-reported success, not confirmed exec. Background launches take no lease. Pinned Rust source and this diagram establish no PTY conformance; real checks remain owed.

diagrams.title: One-session launcher owns entry through final exit
diagrams.caption: Proposed checked protocol, not observed runtime behavior. The front scope survives selection failure and no-ending errors. Child entry values remain immutable; successful release is part of settlement. C4 handback still requires exclusive foreground authority and no unrelated group-identity reuse. A persistent runner remains a separate contract.

diagrams.title: Failed Started transition retains owned teardown
diagrams.caption: Proposed failure sequence through the existing lifecycle observation seam. A mask-restoration error after spawn cannot return until bounded runner cleanup, actual wait and checked terminal recovery have been attempted. All original and secondary reports survive; no result escapes. Remaining readers keep their inherited shield. This sequence is not model checking or runtime evidence.
